q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not drop — they rose. Net sales on 2026-10-13 were ₹91,220 vs ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12 (+127%), so yesterday was a stronger day, not a decline.

What changed (top items, why it matters)
- Orders and basket size: Orders rose 26 → 45 (+73%) and Net AOV rose ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31%) — together these explain the jump in net sales.  
- Ad activity and reach rose: Ad spend ₹38,661 → ₹50,442 (+30%) and impressions 133,023 → 147,290 (+11%). Sessions and add-to-cart events moved up with them, but the data cannot tell whether spend caused the sales uplift or just moved together.  
- Discounts, refunds and deductions increased: Discounts ₹1,553 → ₹5,173 and net sales deductions ₹5,110 → ₹6,569 (both higher), and refund-related lines flagged larger values (refunds rose in the tested comparisons) — these reduce net sales but did not outweigh the orders/AOV increase.  
- Product / campaign signals to check: one ad (TH-471-PLAYSCRATCHLOUNGE_IMG_6516) appeared with +₹24,962 vs usual and some campaigns/ad names dropped to zero (e.g., TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+) — these shifts explain where the volume moved.

Takeaway and certainty
- The data shows an increase, not a drop; no single upstream cause (e.g., a campaign pause or data error) was identified by the diagnostic engine — sessions, add-to-cart and ad spend rose together but causality is not established. Some refunds and discounts were higher and partially offset the gain.

Worth checking: drill to sales by campaign/ad and by product for 2026-10-13 to see which creatives or SKUs drove the order and AOV jump.
